title: Repentance
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Repentance is a grace-shaped turning from sin toward God. True repentance includes sorrow over sin, agreement with God, turning from rebellion, and coming to Him through faith in Christ.
summary: Repentance is a grace-shaped turning from sin toward God. True repentance includes sorrow over sin, agreement with God, turning from rebellion, and coming to Him through faith in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls sinners to repent and receive the kingdom of God. His mercy does not leave sinners hiding in sin, but brings them into forgiveness, restoration, and new obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Repentance is more than regret, embarrassment, fear of consequences, or temporary emotion. It is a real turning of the heart away from sin and toward God.

Scripture holds repentance and faith together. Sinners turn from sin and turn to Christ. Repentance does not earn salvation, but it is part of the response God works in those who receive the Gospel.

Godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation. Worldly sorrow may grieve consequences while still loving sin. True repentance agrees with God’s verdict and seeks mercy in Him.

Repentance continues in the Christian life. Believers still confess sin, turn from what grieves God, and return to the Father who receives repentant sinners through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people confuse repentance with shame. Shame hides and says, “I am beyond return.” Repentance comes into the light and says, “I have sinned, and I need mercy.”

This doctrine is vital for recovery and discipleship because real change is not merely behavior management. God calls people to turn from sin and return to Him in truth and grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice honest repentance before God. Do not excuse sin, rename sin, or let shame drive you into hiding. Confess what God exposes, turn toward Christ, receive mercy, and take practical steps of obedience that match a changed direction.
